subject: Multi-cloud marketplace entry checklist & canary criteria
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Jamie Clark <jamie.clark@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud marketplace entry checklist & canary criteria

Team / Jamie —

We need to finalize the marketplace entry checklist for AWS / Azure / GCP and a small, repeatable canary plan we can run during the first 6 weeks of listing. I uploaded a preliminary SKU matrix (see attachment) that tries to map our 3 packaging tiers (Starter / Scale / Dedicated) across clouds and regions.

High-level asks:
- Confirm which SKUs are acceptable per cloud (tight vs. broad SKU surface).
- Agree on a canary sample (customer segments, regions, traffic %, success metrics).
- Dependencies: co-sell enablement prerequisites (referral program, listing contract items), any legal/procurement items we should pre-seed.
- Owner & timeline: want a lightweight launch checklist by EOD Thu and a 30-min sync with Jamie this week.

Attachments: marketplace-sku-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Director, GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamie Clark <jamie.clark@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace entry checklist & canary criteria

On Mon, Mar 14, 2027 at 09:12 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Jamie —
> 
> We need to finalize the marketplace entry checklist for AWS / Azure / GCP and a small, repeatable canary plan we can run during the first 6 weeks of listing...

Quick pass from product/ops perspective — comments inline and proposed defaults: 

- SKU surface: prefer narrower SKUs at launch (Starter, Scale) and reserve Dedicated for Dedicated marketplace/reserved offerings later. Keep "Dedicated" off initial public catalog to avoid procurement complexity.
- Region priority: US (east/west) -> EU (w/ GDPR review) -> APAC (select zones). For GCP/Azure prioritize zones with existing infra (us-west1/us-central/europe-west1).
- Canary buckets: 3 buckets by traffic size: 1% (smoke, low concurrency), 5% (normal), 20% (stress). Run first 2 weeks smoke + metrics, week 3-6 ramp if p95 latency < 600ms and error rate < 0.5%.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, cold-start percent, cost per 1k tokens (approx).
- Packaging: Offer small hourly SKU + monthly commit SKU for Scale; Starter should be metered only.

I'll attach a short canary-test-plan.md with the metric thresholds and data collection points.

Next steps I propose: 1) Lauren to confirm legal/contract asks we need in listing doc; 2) Marcus to surface pricing/commit thresholds; 3) Soojin to align on co-sell qualification steps with partner ops.

Attachment: canary-test-plan.md

—Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Marketplace
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Jamie Clark <jamie.clark@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace entry checklist & canary criteria

Thanks — quick financial/ops notes: 

- SKU granularity: each public SKU increases catalog churn and billing mapping. Recommend consolidating into 4 public SKUs max for launch (Starter-Metered, Starter-Commit, Scale-Commit, Support-AddOn).
- Pricing guardrails: set list rates intentionally higher than our direct sales committed offers to avoid cannibalization; use Marketplace as demand-gen + self-serve channel.
- Minimum commit: recommend no minimum for Starter; Scale should have a 3-month commit for Marketplace offers to qualify for co-sell rebates.
- Procurement: we need a standard EULA clause for data residency and telemetry retention to satisfy enterprise buyers on marketplace. Lauren, can Legal pre-clear a template to attach to the listing?

I'll volunteer to own the pricing matrix and mapping to billing SKUs if folks are good with the 4 SKU approach.

—Marcus
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Clark <jamie.clark@amazon.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace entry checklist & canary criteria

Hi Lauren / team —

Thanks for the summary. A few operational notes from AWS Marketplace side: 
- Listing requirements: see public doc (https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/listing-requirements). The key items for co-sell referral are (1) clear pricing/schema in the listing, (2) a signed Marketplace Seller Agreement, and (3) telemetry hooks for usage attribution.
- Canaries: we recommend the 1%/5%/20% phased approach. For fast-track co-sell qualification, provide a 4-week canary report with p95, 5xx, and usage attribution mapping.
- Regional coverage: you can publish a single global listing but opt-in to regions you can support. If EU is included, please confirm data residency controls.

Happy to jump on the sync; I'm available Wed or Thu morning PT. I'll loop in the Marketplace partner enablement specialist if you want a pre-check of the listing doc.

—Jamie Clark
Program Manager, AWS Marketplace

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Jamie Clark <jamie.clark@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace entry checklist & canary criteria

Perfect — thanks everyone. Quick decisions and next steps: 

1) SKU set: lean for launch — Marcus will produce the 4-SKU mapping by Wed EOD (owner: Marcus).
2) Canary plan: use Karthik's thresholds; finalize the canary-test-plan.md and instrument telemetry (owner: Karthik).
3) Legal/listing: I'll ask Legal to produce a standard EULA blurb and attach it to the listing draft (owner: Lauren / Legal).
4) Sync: Jamie has availability Wed/Thu mornings PT — Marcus, Karthik, Soojin, please share availability and I'll confirm with Jamie.

I'll file the checklist into the Drive link and create a HubSpot task (see related links).

Thanks —
Lauren
Director, GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference
